knowledge_point.title: Differentiating a Function Using the Chain Rule and Prime Notation

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $g(x)=3 x + 9$ and $f(g(x))=g^{2}.$ 

Differentiating, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(g(x)) & =(g^{2})^{′}=2 g, \\ {g}^{′}(x) & =(3 x + 9)^{′}=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the chain rule, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={f}^{′}(g(x))\cdot {g}^{′}(x) \\  & =(2 g)\cdot (3) \\  & =18 x + 54.\end{aligned}
$$
